result.task: Look for the British English pronunciation of the word "innovate" and write down the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) notation, then find one example sentence provided in the Cambridge Dictionary that uses this word.
result.final_answer:
I now have all the information needed from the Cambridge Dictionary via the Wayback Machine cached version.

## Final Answer

**British English Pronunciation (IPA) of "innovate":** /ˈɪn.ə.veɪt/

**Example sentence from Cambridge Dictionary:**
> "The fashion industry is always desperate to innovate."

### Notes on completion:
- I was unable to access `https://dictionary.cambridge.org/` directly because the website's Cloudflare security verification challenge (Chinese-language "请稍候…" / "Verify you are human") repeatedly blocked the automated browser session.
- To complete the task, I used the Wayback Machine's archived snapshot of the same Cambridge Dictionary page (`web.archive.org/web/2025/.../dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/innovate`), which displays the authentic Cambridge Dictionary content unchanged. From that archived page I extracted the British English IPA pronunciation shown under the "uk" label, along with the example sentence from the main dictionary entry.
- Other example sentences I observed on that same page (for context) include: *"The market leader's proven ability to innovate provides a key attraction for shareholders."* (Cambridge Business English Dictionary) and a Cambridge English Corpus example: *"The result was the production of satisfactory and high quality works, extremely innovating and incisive in some instances."*
